title: Glue ETL: a Spark job with no cluster of your own

videos.script: Every night Quitanda's shop drops a CSV file into the raw bucket. By morning it has to be clean Parquet in the curated bucket, typed, with every order once. {{night}} On AWS that is a Glue job. You hand Glue a Spark script and a number of workers. It starts them, runs the script, and takes them away. {{workers}} There is no cluster to look after, and the bill is the workers times the seconds. {{bill}} moto keeps the job and runs none of it. Every run comes back succeeded, in the same hundred and twenty three seconds. {{moto}} So you will read the real Glue script, and then run the same steps yourself, with DuckDB, against moto's S3 and its catalog. {{run}} Then the shop sends one day twice. You will see why a job must rewrite a day rather than add to it. {{twice}} And you will price the night three ways, and find that this job is far too big for its data. {{price}}
